text:
maia_support: Hi @customer_jones — saw your ticket about 502s to the internal service endpoint, can you confirm this is only from the prod VPC and not from your dev VPC?
customer_jones: Only prod. dev works fine. Errors started ~0800 UTC after a config push.
maia_support: Thanks. Can you paste output of: `dig +short service.prod.internal @169.254.169.253` and `curl -v https://service.prod.internal/health` from a failing pod?
customer_jones: dig: `service.prod.internal` -> 54.210.33.12
customer_jones: curl fails with TLS mismatch: certificate is for service.external.example.com, not service.prod.internal.
ingrid_sre: That looks like split-horizon leak — private hosted zone probably not returning internal IP, falling back to public ALB IP. Which resolver are you using? Any Route53 resolver rules or forwarders?
raj_engineer: We recently attached the org-shared-hostedzone to a different account but not this prod VPC. Also security team enabled egress allowlist last night restricting outbound UDP 53/TCP 53 to a small set of resolver IPs.
maia_support: Can you run `ip netns exec podns dig +trace service.prod.internal` or just `dig @10.0.2.2 service.prod.internal` from the node-local cache? We want to see if node-local is forwarding to the expected resolver.
customer_jones: From pod: `dig @10.0.0.10 service.prod.internal +short` => NXDOMAIN
customer_jones: From host: `dig @172.31.0.2 service.prod.internal +short` => 10.1.5.77 (internal)
ingrid_sre: Interesting — host resolver returns internal IP but pod local DNS returns NXDOMAIN. That implies node-local-dns or coredns config is unable to reach the Route53 resolver it normally talks to. If node-local can't reach the forwarder, it might be failing over to public resolver which gives external ALB IP and leading to cert mismatch.
maia_support: @raj_engineer can you check the egress allowlist logs? Did the security change block the resolver IPs used by kube-proxy/node-local?
raj_engineer: Security confirms they only allowed 198.51.100.5/32 and 198.51.100.6/32; Route53 inbound endpoint IPs are 10.2.4.8/32 (private). Node-local was trying to talk to 10.2.4.8 over UDP/53 and getting reset.
deploy_bot: deploy/egress-allowlist: rolled at 2026-02-11T07:50:12Z — patch #4321 applied to prod VPCs.
ingrid_sre: Root cause: egress allowlist blocked private resolver endpoint for prod VPC's node-local/coredns -> split-horizon failed -> pods saw NXDOMAIN or public fallback. Workaround: add 10.2.4.8/32 to egress allowlist OR re-associate the private hosted zone to prod VPC so queries don't need forwarding.
maia_support: Repro steps documented: 1) From a pod in prod subnet run `dig @10.0.0.10 service.prod.internal +short` (shows NXDOMAIN). 2) From node `dig @10.2.4.8 service.prod.internal +short` (shows 10.1.x.x). 3) Temporarily allow UDP/53 to 10.2.4.8 and confirm pod now resolves to 10.1.x.x and curl returns 200 with matching cert.
raj_engineer: ETA for fix: adding resolver IPs to allowlist now, patch rolling in 5–10m. We'll also add a monitoring alert for node-local NXDOMAIN rate > 1% so this doesn't slip.
customer_jones: Appreciate the quick triage. Are there any long-term mitigations?
ingrid_sre: Long-term: 1) ensure VPC association for private hosted zone in prod to avoid forwarding dependency; 2) publish a required egress IP checklist for infra changes that impact Route53 resolver endpoints; 3) Node-local DNS should fail-open with cached internal answers for short TTLs (engineering followup).
maia_support: I'll update the ticket with the workaround and mark as escalated to eng for the follow-ups. :thumbsup:
